sentences.text: The petitioner is the accused in Crime No.1088/2015 of Palarivattom Police Station, Ernakulam.

The offences alleged against him are under Sections 376, 354D and 294(b) of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, and Section 119(a) of the Kerala Police Act, 2011.  2. The prosecution case is that the accused/petitioner took the de facto complainant to Pondicherry under coercion and indulged in sexual relationship with her against her consent.
The case has been registered pursuant to a complaint preferred by the defacto complainant before the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Kochi City.
3. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that he is totally innocent, and that he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further pointed out that the de facto complainant has filed an affidavit stating that she is not interested in prosecuting the accused for the offences alleged in this case.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.  5.

A copy of the complaint preferred by the de facto complainant before the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Kochi City, is 2025:KER:50119 produced by the petitioner to show that the relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant was purely consensual.

It is categorically stated in the aforesaid complaint that, at the resort in Pondicherry, the petitioner and the defacto complainant indulged in sexual relationship with the full consent of the de facto complainant.
On the subsequent occasion, the petitioner is alleged to have compelled the de facto complainant to have sex with him.
6. At any rate, it is not possible to discern from the above complaint that the petitioner has resorted to force or violence to have sexual relationship with the de facto complainant.
Further, in the affidavit filed by the de facto complainant, it is stated by her in unequivocal terms that the coitus between her and the petitioner was purely consensual.

It is further stated by the defacto complainant in the said affidavit that she has no objection in quashing the proceedings against the petitioner, since the matter has been amicably settled between them.
7. Having regard to the above facts and circumstances of this case, it is not possible to say that the petitioner has committed any of the offences, as alleged against him.
In that view of the matter, the prayer in this petition to quash the proceedings against him, has to be 2025:KER:50119 allowed.
In the result, the petition stands allowed.

The Annexure-1 FIR registered by the Palarivattom Police in Crime No.1088 of 2015 and all proceedings initiated against the petitioner pursuant to the above registration of the crime, are hereby quashed.

sd/ G.GIRISH,JUDGE jm/
